title: stopAfterDelay(d, unit) truncates sub-millisecond limits with toMillis, so Retryer.call stops before the delay elapses (sub-ms limit: one attempt only)
cause: StopStrategies.stopAfterDelay(long, TimeUnit) converts the limit with timeUnit.toMillis(duration), which truncates toward zero, and StopAfterDelayStrategy.shouldStop returns getDelaySinceFirstAttempt() >= maxDelay; the effective stop condition is elapsed >= floor(limit in ms), so any sub-millisecond part of the limit is dropped and a limit below 1 ms becomes 0.
trigger: A Retryer built through public API with StopStrategies.stopAfterDelay(d, MICROSECONDS or NANOSECONDS) where d has a sub-millisecond part (e.g. 500 us, 999_999 ns, 1900 us), and an attempt that is rejected (exception or rejected result) before the configured delay has elapsed.
consequence: Retryer.call (and RetryerCallable/Future.get) throws RetryException before the configured delay has elapsed: for a sub-ms limit after the first failed attempt (about 2 us elapsed; the attempt that would have returned a value never runs), in general up to 0.999 ms early, contrary to the Javadoc 'has exceeded the given delay amount'.
premises: stopAfterDelay(long, TimeUnit) accepts every TimeUnit; no precondition rejects or rounds sub-millisecond values (only maxDelay >= 0 is checked after conversion).
Retryer.call computes the delay as NANOSECONDS.toMillis(nanoTime - startTime) and throws RetryException as soon as shouldStop returns true; no library mechanism re-attempts or recovers afterwards.
Reproduced at Level 0 (public API only) against guava-retrying 2.0.0 (177b6c9) compiled unmodified with Guava 22.0 and jsr305 2.0.2 on JDK 21 with --release 8.
